t: Count Tested Devices After Test Operations
o: Scanning devices left to right, each device with positive remaining battery gets tested and drains 1 from every later device. Naive simulation is O(n²); since n ≤ 100 that's fine, but the drain applied to later devices is uniform, so we can track the cumulative number of tests so far and compare it against each battery in O(n).
k: Device i's battery at its turn equals batteryPercentages[i] minus the number of tests performed before i.
So device i is tested iff batteryPercentages[i] > (tests so far); no array mutation is needed.

a.i: Literally perform the described operations: when testing device i, decrement all subsequent batteries clamped at 0. Matches the statement exactly and is trivially correct for tiny n.
s: For each i: if battery[i] > 0, count++ and decrement all j > i (clamped at 0).
a.t: O(n²) — each test decrements up to n devices

a.i: Every prior test subtracts exactly 1 from device i, so instead of mutating, keep a counter t of tests done; device i is tested iff batteryPercentages[i] − t > 0. This removes the inner loop entirely.
s: For each i: if batteryPercentages[i] > t, increment t.

w: Always offer the counter trick — it turns an easy simulation into a one-liner and demonstrates recognizing uniform deferred updates. Pitfall: the comparison is strict (> t), since a battery drained to exactly the number of prior tests is 0. Follow-up: what if tests drain batteries by varying amounts?
